name: Hathi Grey
lede: Hathi Grey is a soft greenish grey that Ridgway standardized in 1912, and our archive finds a close match in roughly one painting in thirty-four.

sections.title: A 1912 standard with an undocumented word
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* places Hathi Grey on plate LII, hue 35 (five primes), tone b [1]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files it as a greenish gray, block 155, the same descriptive term as our own [[greenish-grey]] entry; Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary cites that same ISCC-NBS circular rather than giving an independent record [1]. Why 'hathi' was chosen is undocumented in the sources we checked [1].

The closest common color word in our library is [[grey|Grey]] itself, about eight units away in CIEDE2000 [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
A color within six units of Hathi Grey covers at least five percent of the canvas in 699 of our 23,781 paintings, 2.94 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 430 [2]. That ranks it ahead of 81 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It most often plays a light, in 47 percent of its 430 appearances [2].

Henri Matisse is its most devoted painter, in nine of his 50 paintings here, 6.9 times the rate of the museums those works come from [2]. It shares canvases with [[deep-neutral-grey|Deep Neutral Grey]] and [[french-grey|French Grey]] more than chance would predict, with lifts of 6.5 and 4.6 [2]. The earliest matching painting dates to 1399, 513 years before Ridgway recorded the name in 1912 — a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof the color existed as a pigment that early, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
